title: Battery Endurance and Essential Network Behaviour for Extended Diversion Operations
abstract: Operator request to extend the demonstrated battery endurance of the essential network so that a 240-minute diversion can be planned without carrying an operational restriction on the northern routes.

sections.request: We are moving our transatlantic and polar schedules onto longer diversion times and our operations people have found that the limiting item is no longer fuel or the engines but the battery. The way it stands, we have to plan the northern routes with a shorter diversion allowance than the airframe would otherwise support, which costs us track miles on about forty rotations a month. We would like the demonstrated endurance of the essential network raised so that the operational restriction can be lifted. We are not asking for a bigger battery if there is another way. Our engineers think a lot of the endurance is lost to loads that nobody actually needs after the generators have gone, and if those could be shed automatically we would be happy with that answer.
sections.background: Two of our aircraft were used for a monitored trial last year in which the essential network was run down on the ground with a representative load. The results were below the planning figure by a margin we could not explain, and the shop found that both charge limiters were passing a trickle current into a heated element that should have been shed. The current standard was cut in during production and we do not know which of our aircraft carry it.
sections.expected_outcome: A demonstrated essential network endurance that supports the longer diversion allowance without an operational restriction, an unambiguous way of telling from the aircraft records which standard is fitted, and no increase in the scheduled battery capacity check workload.

type_data.business_justification: The shorter diversion allowance costs track miles on roughly forty rotations a month and blocks two planned polar routings; the trial data suggests the shortfall is recoverable without additional battery capacity.
